subject: pharmacology
title: Chloramphenicol, Gray Baby Syndrome, Aplastic Anaemia and the Macrolide Bridge

steps.tx: **Chloramphenicol** blocks the 50S peptidyl transferase reaction with beautiful breadth (Gram positives, negatives, anaerobes, rickettsiae) and CNS penetration that once made it meningitis royalty, before its haematological price retired it wherever alternatives exist. It remains in topical eye preparations (where systemic exposure is trivial and debate continues), resource limited typhoid and meningitis niches, and Rocky Mountain spotted fever pregnancy alternatives by specialist judgement.
steps.say: Chloramphenicol does everything and is forgiven almost nothing; the marrow writes its formulary status.

left.title: Chloramphenicol virtues
points: 50S blockade, broad and bactericidal against key pathogens

right.title: Why it retired
points: Safer rivals for every first world indication
Levels and blood counts where used systemically

steps.tx: **Gray baby syndrome** is neonatal pharmacokinetics made visible: immature hepatic glucuronidation and renal excretion accumulate chloramphenicol, which poisons mitochondrial protein synthesis (mammalian ribosomes resemble bacterial), producing ashen grey cyanosis, abdominal distension, hypothermia, vasomotor collapse and death in the first days of dosed life. Weight based neonatal dosing caps and level monitoring were written from this syndrome, and its mechanism previews mitochondrial toxicities across the antibiotic cabinet.
steps.say: The gray baby is a metabolism lesson: no conjugation, mitochondrial poisoning, grey collapse.

nodes.label: Ashen cyanosis, distension and cardiovascular collapse

steps.tx: **Aplastic anaemia** after chloramphenicol divides into two diseases students must separate: a dose dependent, reversible marrow suppression (reticulocytopenia, rising serum iron) monitored by counts during therapy, and an idiosyncratic, dose independent aplasia (roughly 1 in 25,000 to 40,000 courses) appearing weeks to months after exposure, often fatal and the reason the drug is banned from casual use even topically in some jurisdictions' anxieties.
steps.say: Reversible suppression is dose; aplasia is destiny at one in thirty thousand, and only the second retired the drug.

right.title: Idiosyncratic aplasia
points: Dose independent, delayed weeks to months
No monitoring can prevent it: avoidance does

steps.tx: **Erythromycin**, the original macrolide, binds the 50S exit tunnel and blocks translocation, covering atypicals (Legionella, Mycoplasma, Chlamydia), Campylobacter, Bordetella and penicillin allergic streptococcal niches, while its motilin agonism (next lesson) makes gastrointestinal misery its signature and intravenous phlebitis its rite. Its CYP3A4 inhibition and QT effects preview clarithromycin's fuller treatment next lesson; here it stands as the class founder whose inconveniences successors engineered away.
steps.say: Erythromycin founded the macrolides and billed in cramps; successors kept the ribosome and fired the gut.

steps.tx: **Azithromycin** re engineered erythromycin into tissue: a 15 member azalide concentrating intracellularly and in phagocytes with a 68 hour half life permitting single dose chlamydia therapy, three to five day respiratory courses and once weekly prophylaxis (MAC in advanced HIV historically). Its QT effect exists but CYP inhibition is minor beside clarithromycin's, and mass drug administration for trachoma and childhood mortality programmes made it public health infrastructure in the tropics.
steps.say: Azithromycin lives in tissues for days after the course ends; short courses, long shadows.

left.title: Azithromycin profile
points: Single dose chlamydia, short respiratory courses

right.title: Azithromycin cautions
points: Hearing effects at high prolonged doses
Infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis signal early in life

steps.tx: **Macrolide resistance travels** by two roads, efflux (mef, low level) and ribosomal methylation (erm, high level and inducible, making clindamycin falsely susceptible unless the D test unmasks it in the laboratory). Pneumococcal macrolide resistance above 25 percent in many regions retired macrolide monotherapy for pneumonia where bacteraemia threatens, a stewardship arithmetic repeated with every generation of this family since erythromycin's debut.
steps.say: Efflux whispers resistance, methylation shouts it, and the D test catches clindamycin lying.

nodes.label: Inducible clindamycin resistance unmasked by D test

steps.tx: **Chloramphenicol's surviving systemic** niches are geography and desperation: typhoid fever where fluoroquinolone and ceftriaxone resistance circles back (with its own resistance history read first), bacterial meningitis in beta lactam catastrophe settings, brain abscess anaerobic cover in resource limited theatres, and topical ocular therapy everywhere. Each niche is a place where its marrow price buys something alternatives locally cannot, never a preference where they can.
steps.say: Chloramphenicol survives where resistance or poverty closes every other door, and nowhere else.

left.title: Surviving niches
points: Meningitis where beta lactams are impossible

steps.tx: **Drug interactions complete** chloramphenicol: it inhibits CYP enzymes and prolongs phenytoin, sulfonylurea, warfarin and cyclosporine effects, while rifampicin induction collapses its levels and phenobarbital does both directions in sequence. In the resource limited theatres where it survives, these interactions are managed by levels and vigilance rather than formulary exile, the pragmatic pharmacology of places whose alternatives are stockouts.
steps.say: Chloramphenicol slows everyone else's metabolism while inducers erase its own; levels arbitrate.
